name: Austin
operatingHours: CapMetro Rail Red Line (Downtown–Leander) runs Mon–Thu ~5:00 AM–~8:00 PM and Fri ~5:00 AM–midnight, every ~15–30 min at peaks and less often off-peak; Sat ~10:00 AM–midnight; no Sunday service. Buses and MetroRapid fill the gaps, and late-night Night Owl buses run after midnight.
fareInfo: Red Line rides use the Commuter fare: $3.50 a ride, capped at $7.00 per day (2026). Local buses, including Route 20 to the airport, are $1.25, capped at $2.50 per day. Pay in the Umo app, with a CapMetro Reloadable Fare Card, or by tapping a contactless card or phone (daily capping only); at least one ticket machine stays at each rail station. Under-18s ride free. Fares rise on 10 Jan 2027 (Commuter $4.00, Local $1.50).

sights.name: Texas State Capitol
sights.note: The pink-granite 1888 capitol, taller than the U.S. Capitol, with a soaring rotunda dome and free guided tours.
sights.hours: Mon–Fri 7:00 AM–8:00 PM, Sat–Sun 9:00 AM–8:00 PM; free tours every 15–30 min until 4:15 PM

sights.name: Barton Springs Pool
sights.note: A spring-fed natural pool in Zilker Park that stays around 68°F (20°C) all year.
sights.hours: 5:00 AM–10:00 PM daily; closed Thu 9:00 AM–7:00 PM for cleaning

sights.name: LBJ Presidential Library
sights.note: Lyndon B. Johnson's presidential library on the UT campus, covering civil rights, Vietnam and a replica Oval Office.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–5:00 PM daily (last entry 4:00 PM); half price on Tuesdays

sights.name: Lady Bird Lake Hike-and-Bike Trail
sights.note: A 10-mile loop path around the downtown reservoir, with skyline views, kayak rentals and the Pfluger pedestrian bridge.

sights.name: Mount Bonnell
sights.note: A short stair climb to one of the city's highest points, looking over the Colorado River and Pennybacker Bridge; popular at sunset.

sights.name: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center
sights.note: The University of Texas botanic garden of native plants and wildflowers, about 16 km southwest of downtown (car or rideshare).
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–5:00 PM daily, last entry 4:00 PM (Jun–Aug 7:00 AM–3:00 PM)

sights.name: Bullock Texas State History Museum
sights.note: Three floors telling the story of Texas, from early peoples and the 17th-century La Belle shipwreck to the oil age, plus an IMAX theatre.

sights.name: Congress Avenue Bridge Bats
sights.note: About 1.5 million Mexican free-tailed bats fly out from under the bridge at dusk, the largest urban bat colony in North America.
sights.hours: Around sunset, roughly March–October (peak August); few bats after early November

sights.name: Zilker Metropolitan Park
sights.note: Austin's 350-acre central park, with a great lawn, canoe rentals, a miniature train and the Barton Springs pool.

sights.name: South Congress Avenue
sights.note: SoCo, a strip of vintage shops, boot stores, food trucks and live-music bars with a view up Congress to the Capitol.
sights.hours: Street always open; shops ~10:00 AM–7:00 PM, bars later

sights.name: McKinney Falls State Park
sights.note: Limestone ledges and waterfalls on Onion Creek, with swimming holes and trails, about 13 km southeast of downtown (car needed).
sights.hours: 8:00 AM–10:00 PM daily; reserve a $6 day pass, the park often fills

sights.name: Blanton Museum of Art
sights.note: UT's art museum, with European and Latin American collections and Ellsworth Kelly's chapel-like building 'Austin'.
sights.hours: Tue–Fri & Sun 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, Sat to 8:00 PM, closed Mon; free on Tuesdays

sights.name: Zilker Botanical Garden
sights.note: Themed gardens beside Zilker Park, including a Japanese garden, a rose garden and a dinosaur-footprint trail.
sights.hours: 9:00 AM–5:00 PM daily, last entry 4:30 PM (Jun–Aug 8:00 AM–4:00 PM); closed on ACL Festival weekends

sights.name: I Love You So Much Mural
sights.note: A hand-painted love note on the wall of Jo's Coffee on South Congress, one of the city's most photographed spots.
sights.hours: Outdoors, always visible; queues at weekends

sights.name: Rainey Street
sights.note: Old bungalows turned into bars with big porches and food trucks, a busy nightlife strip a short walk from the convention center.
sights.hours: Bars ~4:00 PM–2:00 AM, busiest Thu–Sat nights

sights.name: Harry Ransom Center
sights.note: UT's free rare-books museum, which shows a Gutenberg Bible and the world's first photograph, plus changing literary and film exhibitions.
sights.hours: Tue–Fri 10:00 AM–5:00 PM, Sat–Sun noon–5:00 PM, closed Mon; free

railStations.name: Austin Amtrak Station
railStations.note: Amtrak's Texas Eagle stops here once a day each way: north to Dallas, St. Louis and Chicago, south to San Antonio, with through cars to Los Angeles three times a week. It is on North Lamar west of downtown, not on the Red Line; downtown is a ~15-min walk or a short bus ride.
railStations.hours: One train each way daily (~9 AM northbound, ~5 PM southbound); the waiting room opens around train times.

airports.name: Austin-Bergstrom International Airport
airports.transitNote: CapMetro bus Route 20 (not on this map) runs from the Barbara Jordan Terminal arrivals level every ~15 min to downtown (~30 min) and UT for the $1.25 local fare. Taxi or rideshare to downtown is ~20 min. The Project Connect Blue Line light rail to the airport is still years away.
airports.hours: Route 20: ~5:00 AM–~midnight; Night Owl Route 483 runs after midnight, six nights a week.
